text.en: Cousin Ravi's wedding. The relatives expect you, the earning one, to give ₹50,000. "Use a [[credit_card]]. Easy monthly payments!" says an uncle.

truth.en: Easy to start. At 42% a year, ₹50,000 costs about ₹12,000 in interest over 12 months.

label.en: Give ₹10,000 with love, and help cook for 300 guests

outcome.en: ₹10,000, no debt. Your uncle grumbles for one day. Then he eats your sambar and goes quiet.

why.en: Family duties matter. Give from your budget, not from a loan.

label.en: Put ₹50,000 of gifts and clothes on the credit card

hint.en: Everyone remembers the gift for a week. The card remembers for a year.

outcome.en: Everyone praises you for an evening. The ₹50,000 costs about ₹62,000 by the time it's paid.

why.en: When income grows, spending to impress grows faster. That's lifestyle inflation.

label.en: Skip the wedding to save money

outcome.en: You save ₹10,000 and lose a lot of love. Ammamma: "Money is for people, kanna."

why.en: Being too stingy also costs something. A budget includes people.

text.en: Nanna's back is weak now. Chinni is in college. Four offers on the table. A [[mudra]] loan is "collateral-free", says the bank.

truth.en: No property is pledged, but the EMI is still yours. Missing it hurts your [[credit_score]].

label.en: Move to Hyderabad for a better job

outcome.en: ₹26,000 a month. Rent ₹7,000, ₹5,000 home to Amma. You still save ₹4,000 more than before.

why.en: More pay brings more costs. Count what's left after rent and family, not the salary.

label.en: A Gulf job through a licensed recruiting agent

hint.en: You'll see Chinni's graduation on a video call.

outcome.en: ₹40,000 a month, but ₹15,000 goes on living costs there. You send ₹15,000 home.

why.en: Money sent home is love, but plan it. Remittances need a budget too.

label.en: Stay and grow the farm with Nanna

outcome.en: About ₹14,000 a month, more in a good season. Crop insurance and a [[kcc]] at 7%. Bujji approves.

why.en: Lower income can still be a good life if costs are low and risks are insured.

label.en: Start a small repair shop with a Mudra loan

outcome.en: ₹1 lakh at about 10% is ₹2,125 a month for 5 years. You earn ₹18,000 in a good month, ₹9,000 in a bad one.

why.en: Business income goes up and down. Keep the EMI small enough for the bad months.

text.en: TV anchors are shouting. Your index fund shows ₹29,400. Last month it was ₹42,000. A WhatsApp tip says "sell everything, buy this sure-shot share".

truth.en: Nobody knows the bottom. One share can fall far more than a whole index.

label.en: Keep the SIP running. Don't sell

outcome.en: Your SIP buys more units cheaply. In this world, two years later your fund is back above ₹48,000.

why.en: Crashes are normal. Selling in panic turns a paper loss into a real one.

label.en: Sell everything before it falls more

outcome.en: You lock in a ₹12,600 loss. The market recovers in 20 months, without you.

why.en: Missing the recovery is the most expensive part of panic-selling.

label.en: Sell and put it all into the sure-shot share

hint.en: All your eggs, one basket, no basket.

outcome.en: The "sure-shot" share falls 60%. Your ₹29,400 is now ₹11,800.

why.en: [[diversification]] protects you. One company can collapse; a whole index rarely does.

text.en: A colleague whispers: "Put all your savings in this one share. My cousin says it will triple. Can't lose." You have ₹30,000 saved.

truth.en: Every investment can lose. A single share can fall to almost nothing.

label.en: Spread it: some in FD, some gold, some in an index fund

outcome.en: When the market falls 30% next year, your ₹30,000 dips only about ₹3,500 overall.

why.en: [[diversification]]: different things fall at different times, so one bad year hurts less.

label.en: Put all ₹30,000 in the one share

hint.en: His cousin is suddenly very hard to reach.

outcome.en: The share halves in six months. ₹30,000 becomes ₹15,000. The colleague changes jobs.

why.en: All your savings in one thing means one bad day can take half of it.

label.en: Keep it all as cash at home

outcome.en: No crash can touch it. But 6% inflation quietly takes ₹1,800 of its value this year.

why.en: Avoiding all risk has its own cost: slow loss to inflation.

text.en: Three days of rain. The village tank breaks its bank. Crop and house wall damaged: ₹80,000. Bujji is fine, standing on the roof of her shed.

truth.en: Crop insurance, a health card and an emergency fund decide how much of this you pay.

label.en: Claim insurance, use the emergency fund, borrow only the gap cheaply

outcome.en: Insurance pays first, then your fund. Whatever you prepared shrinks the ₹80,000 hit.

why.en: Calamities can't be avoided. Their damage can be made smaller, before they happen.

label.en: Apply for flood relief first, then pay the rest

outcome.en: Two weeks of forms with {cast:banker}'s help. ₹10,000 of government relief arrives. ₹70,000 left to cover.

why.en: Government relief exists for disasters. Ask for it, and keep every receipt.

label.en: Go straight to the sahukar, keep your savings

hint.en: Ammamma stares at the sahukar's house for a long time.

outcome.en: Your savings stay. At ₹2 per ₹100 a month, the ₹80,000 costs ₹99,200 to clear in a year.

why.en: Savings that sit unused while you pay a sahukar are costing you money.

text.en: {cast:agent} arrives at lunchtime. "Golden Future Plan! ₹30,000 a year for 15 years. Guaranteed ₹6 lakh, plus ₹3 lakh life cover. Free steel dinner set!"

truth.en: You pay ₹4.5 lakh over 15 years. Getting ₹6 lakh back is only about 3.5% a year.
Too small to protect a family. A [[term_insurance]] plan gives ₹50 lakh for about ₹11,000 a year.
Paid from your premium. His [[commission]] can be about ₹9,000 of your first year.

label.en: Sign up for the Golden Future Plan

hint.en: The dinner set is shiny. The lock-in is 15 years.

outcome.en: ₹30,000 a year, locked for 15 years, earning about 3.5%. Ramana leaves with the last vada.

why.en: Mixed plans pay big commissions and give low cover. Keep insurance and investing separate.

label.en: Buy cheap term cover and invest the rest yourself

outcome.en: ₹11,000 a year buys ₹50 lakh of cover. ₹19,000 a year in an index fund could reach ₹5–7 lakh in 15 years.

why.en: Pure cover protects the family. A low-fee fund grows the money. Each does one job well.

label.en: Ask Ramana how much he earns from this

outcome.en: He laughs, eats the last vada, and admits it: about ₹9,000 from your first year.

why.en: Always ask how the seller is paid. It explains what they push.

text.en: {cast:tempter}'s sunglasses are now enormous. "Lucky Wealth Club! Guaranteed double in 12 months. Risk-free. Bonus for every friend you bring!"

truth.en: That's 100% a year. Honest savings pay about 7%. Nobody honest can promise this.
High return and no risk never go together.

phrase.en: Bonus for every friend you bring!

truth.en: Old members are paid with new members' money. That's a [[ponzi]]. It always collapses.

label.en: Put in ₹50,000

outcome.en: You pay ₹50,000. Three monthly "returns" of ₹4,000 arrive. You feel very smart.

why.en: Early payouts are bait, paid with newer members' money. They stop when new money stops.

label.en: Put in ₹50,000 and bring Chintu and two cousins

hint.en: Three families now trust your word.

outcome.en: ₹12,000 in returns and ₹6,000 in bonuses. Your cousins put in ₹1.5 lakh because of you.

why.en: Recruiting into a Ponzi makes you part of it. The law and your family will both ask.

label.en: Refuse, and warn the village through Kavitha akka's SHG

outcome.en: 100% a year is impossible. Your warning keeps ₹3 lakh of SHG savings out of the club.

why.en: If it sounds too good to be true, it is. Ask: where does the profit really come from?

text.en: A man in uniform on video: "A drugs parcel is in your name. You are under digital arrest. Don't tell anyone. Transfer ₹60,000 for verification."

truth.en: There is no such thing. Real police never arrest or collect money on a video call.
Scammers isolate you so no one can stop you. Tell someone at once.

label.en: Hang up and call 1930

outcome.en: 1930 confirms it's a known scam. ₹60,000 safe. You post a warning in the family group.

why.en: [[digital_arrest]] scams run on fear. Hanging up is always allowed.

label.en: Pay, to clear your name

hint.en: They will call again. They always call again.

outcome.en: ₹60,000 gone. Then they demand ₹1 lakh more. You call 1930, late, and ₹15,000 is frozen.

why.en: Paying never ends it. Police don't take money to "verify" anyone.

label.en: Say you'll call back, and phone Chinni first

outcome.en: Chinni: "That's a scam! A patient's son lost ₹2 lakh to it." ₹60,000 safe.

why.en: Talking to one trusted person breaks the scammer's spell.

text.en: {cast:friend} is a delivery rider now, out of his loan-app mess. "Mama, how do I make sure I never end up there again?"

label.en: "Build three months of expenses in a separate account first"

outcome.en: He starts a ₹1,000 RD. In two years he has ₹24,000, and stops panicking when the bike breaks.

why.en: An emergency fund is what stands between a bad day and a loan app.

label.en: "Get a credit card for emergencies"

outcome.en: His first emergency goes on the card at 42%. He's back where he started within a year.

why.en: A credit card is borrowing, not a cushion. Savings are the cushion.

label.en: "Buy a little gold every month"

outcome.en: He buys ₹1,000 of gold a month. Selling it in a hurry costs him 10% in charges.

why.en: Gold is fine for long-term savings. Emergencies need cash you can reach today.

text.en: {cast:sibling} is a staff nurse now, earning ₹22,000. "Should I invest now, or wait till I earn more like you?"

label.en: "Emergency fund first, then a small SIP now. Time matters most."

outcome.en: She starts ₹1,500 a month at 25. If it averages 10%, that's about ₹6 lakh by 40.

why.en: Starting early beats starting big. She has 15 years of compounding on her side.

label.en: "Put it all in one share a doctor told me about"

outcome.en: The share falls 40%. Chinni loses ₹8,000 and stops investing for three years.

why.en: One share is a gamble. Spread money out, and keep costs low.

label.en: "Wait. You don't earn enough yet."

outcome.en: She waits five years. Starting at 30 instead of 25 roughly halves what she'd have at 40.

why.en: Waiting for a big salary costs the years compounding needs.

text.en: You need ₹40,000 urgently. You've paid ₹60,000 into the Golden Future Plan. Its surrender value today: ₹18,000.

label.en: Surrender it and take ₹18,000

outcome.en: You lose ₹42,000. Then you buy term cover and an RD, separately.

why.en: Long lock-ins with heavy early charges punish people who need their money.

label.en: Keep paying and borrow elsewhere

outcome.en: Another ₹30,000 premium, plus a loan for the ₹40,000 you needed.

why.en: Throwing good money after a bad product is still throwing money.

text.en: The Lucky Wealth Club office is locked. Phones off. 2,000 members, ₹40 crore gone. Your ₹38,000 is gone too.

label.en: File a police complaint with other victims

outcome.en: Years later, the court returns part of the seized money: ₹6,000 of your ₹38,000.

why.en: Complaining together helps police seize assets. Some money comes back; most doesn't.

label.en: Pay ₹20,000 "release fee" a caller asks for

hint.en: Scammers keep lists of people who already paid.

outcome.en: The "recovery agent" is another scammer. ₹20,000 more is gone.

why.en: Victims get targeted again with fake recovery offers. Only police and courts recover money.

text.en: The club collapses. Your cousins lost ₹1.5 lakh because you vouched for it. The police list you as a recruiter.

label.en: Cooperate with police and repay your cousins what you can

outcome.en: You give a full statement and return your ₹6,000 bonus, plus ₹24,000 to your cousins. It's a start.

why.en: The way back is honesty and repair. It costs money now and saves your name later.

label.en: Say you were only a victim too

outcome.en: The bonus payments to your account say otherwise. The case drags on. Your cousins stop visiting.

why.en: Taking bonuses for bringing people in made you part of it. Owning that is the way back.

text.en: Immigration checks your experience certificate. Fake. Your visa is cancelled. The agent's number is switched off. The ₹1.2 lakh loan remains.

label.en: Tell the truth and file a complaint against the agent

outcome.en: You're let go with a warning. Police find the agent cheated 40 others. You start repaying the ₹1.2 lakh.

why.en: Fake documents can ban you from travel for years. Licensed agents never sell papers.

label.en: Find another agent with "better" papers

hint.en: The second fake is easier to catch than the first.

outcome.en: ₹40,000 more, another rejection, and your name on a watch list.

why.en: A shortcut that failed once fails worse the second time. The way back is the truth.

text.en: You claim ₹35,000 for Amma's knee surgery. The insurer refuses: "Existing illness, four-year waiting period. Page 11."

label.en: Appeal, then complain to the insurance ombudsman

outcome.en: The rule was real, so the claim stays rejected. But you learn to read page 11 first.

why.en: Waiting periods and exclusions decide what a policy really covers. Read them before paying.

label.en: Give up on insurance forever

hint.en: One bad policy doesn't make all cover bad.

outcome.en: You pay ₹35,000 and cancel every policy, including the good ones.

why.en: The fix for a bad policy is a better one, not none.

text.en: The [[chit]] organiser's house is locked. Twenty families, ₹5,000 a month each. Your ₹60,000 of payments is gone.

label.en: File a joint police complaint with the other members

outcome.en: Police trace him in a year. Members get back about 20%: ₹12,000 for you.

why.en: Registered chits have a registrar who holds security money. Unregistered ones have only trust.

label.en: Let it go

outcome.en: ₹60,000 gone. Amma stops trusting anyone with a notebook, except Anjamma aunty.

text.en: Your loan statement shows a ₹3,500 "loan insurance" and a 4% fee if you repay early. Both were in the papers.

label.en: Write to the lender and ask for the add-on to be removed

outcome.en: They cancel the insurance after a month of letters. You lose ₹1,500 and learn to read clause 7.

label.en: Just pay it

outcome.en: ₹3,500 for something you never chose.

text.en: One EMI late. The lender's agents call Amma, Chinni and your boss. The papers you signed allowed "contacting references".

label.en: Pay the EMI and report the harassment to the bank regulator and police

outcome.en: The ₹2,000 late EMI is paid, and the calls stop after your complaint. Recovery agents can't threaten anyone.

why.en: Even when you owe money, harassment is illegal. Complain to the lender, the regulator and police.

label.en: Take another app loan to pay this one

hint.en: Two apps, then three. This is how Chintu's year went.

outcome.en: One loan pays another. Within three months you owe four apps ₹28,000.

why.en: Borrowing to repay borrowing is a trap. Talk to the lender or a bank instead.

text.en: An agent, sent by {cast:tempter}: "₹1.2 lakh fee. We will make your experience certificate. Visit visa now, work visa there."

phrase.en: We will make your experience certificate.

truth.en: That's a fake document. Using it can mean a cancelled visa, a travel ban and a police case.

phrase.en: Visit visa now, work visa there.

truth.en: Working on a visit visa is illegal. Licensed agents give a work visa and contract before you fly.

label.en: Borrow ₹1.2 lakh and take the deal

hint.en: A certificate for a job you never did.

outcome.en: ₹1,77,600 to repay the sahukar. A ticket is booked. The certificate is from a company that doesn't exist.

label.en: Check his licence on the government's list of recruiting agents

outcome.en: He's not on the list. ₹1.2 lakh saved. You report him, and help two neighbours avoid him too.

label.en: Refuse. It feels wrong

outcome.en: You walk away ₹0 poorer. Months later the agent is arrested for cheating 40 people.

text.en: {cast:sibling} got a seat in B.Sc Nursing! Fees: ₹60,000 a year for four years. She looks at you. Everyone looks at you.

phrase.en: Fees: ₹60,000 a year for four years.

truth.en: ₹2.4 lakh in total. An education loan with you as co-borrower spreads it over 7 years.

label.en: Education loan in her name, with you as co-borrower

outcome.en: About ₹5,700 a month once repayment starts, as interest adds up while she studies. A staff nurse earns ₹22,000. Chinni hugs Bujji.

why.en: An education loan is good debt when the course leads to steady work.

label.en: Borrow from Narsaiah sahukar, it's faster

outcome.en: ₹74,400 to repay the sahukar, for one year's fees. Three more years to go.

label.en: Ask her to work for a year first

outcome.en: Chinni cries quietly and takes a ₹6,000 hospital helper job. The seat goes to someone else.

text.en: No rain in July. No rain in August. The cotton dries in the field. The family loses ₹40,000 of crop.

label.en: Claim crop insurance and use savings

outcome.en: Crop insurance pays first, if you had it. Savings cover the rest. Nanna sleeps that night.

label.en: Borrow from the sahukar for next season

hint.en: This is how the story began, last time.

outcome.en: ₹49,600 to repay in a year. Next season must be perfect. Ammamma doesn't sleep.

text.en: Amma's friend runs a ₹1 lakh [[chit]]: 20 members, ₹5,000 a month. "No registration needed, we all trust each other."

phrase.en: No registration needed, we all trust each other.

truth.en: Chits must be registered with the state registrar. Unregistered organisers can vanish with the pot.

label.en: Join a registered chit instead, after checking its papers

outcome.en: ₹5,000 a month in a registered chit. The organiser keeps about 5% as commission. Your money is traceable.

label.en: Join the friend's chit

hint.en: Trust is lovely. Receipts are better.

outcome.en: ₹5,000 a month, no receipts. Everyone is very friendly.

label.en: Skip it, start a ₹5,000 RD at the bank

outcome.en: ₹5,000 a month at about 6.5%. Boring, safe, and Amma's friend sulks.

text.en: Cotton prices jump. The family earns ₹25,000 more than expected. Nanna wants a big TV. Amma wants to clear the kirana khata.

label.en: Clear the khata, save the rest for the emergency fund

outcome.en: ₹5,000 clears the khata. Anjamma aunty crosses out a page she's kept for 12 years. ₹20,000 saved.

label.en: Big TV and a feast

hint.en: Good seasons are for saving for bad ones.

outcome.en: ₹25,000 becomes a TV the whole street watches cricket on. The khata stays open.
